correctness.rationale: Each transverse monomial slice reduces the operator, with squared moments n! r!/(n+r)! after a constant rescaling. For r>=1 its operator is exactly Miller's C_nu with Bergman weight parameter r-1 and nu=r+1. The cited disk and Fredholm boundary apply at these parameters, and subnormality gives norm 2/(r+1). Independently, for the Hardy block C=G_0, its matrix gives (C-I)(C-I)^*=I-diag(1/(n+1)): CC^* has entry 1/(max(i,j)+1). This implies closed range of C-I of codimension one; the forward coefficient recurrence gives injectivity. Thus C-I is Fredholm and its Calkin image is unitary, so failure-of-Fredholm points lie on the circle. Its index is -1 at the center and 0 outside the unit disk about the center, by Hardy disk spectrum; local constancy of index forces every point of the circle into the failure set. For all r, the forward recurrence gives squared weighted coefficients of order n^(r+2n0) for any putative first nonzero degree n0, excluding eigenvectors, and the zero parameter is excluded by invertibility of the formal triangular recurrence. The adjoint recurrence has at most one free coefficient: with h_n=sqrt(w_n)g_n, h_(n+1)=(1-1/(conj(lambda)(n+r+1)))h_n. Any square-summable candidate solves the adjoint equation by telescoping since h_n tends to zero. Finite-support resonances lie strictly inside the disk; otherwise summability is exactly 2 Re(1/lambda)>r+1 by the product power asymptotics. At nonzero lambda the norm-decaying tail is uniformly invertible by the Neumann bound; a circle block prevents Fredholmness, as does the Hardy block at zero. Off the circles the finite sum of block defects for 0<=r<k yields the stated binomial by the stars-and-bars multiplicities and hockey-stick identity. This also gives the x^(1-d) growth with the stated constant. The ordinary spectrum equals the largest block disk by the same uniform tail argument and presence of the Hardy block. The included finite checker was read, not executed; it does not establish the infinite-dimensional conclusions.
residual_risks: Uses the cited weighted-Bergman one-block spectral theorem, not a new proof of it; Fredholm means invertible in the Calkin algebra, not the Weyl or Browder convention.
